justification: Regression guard for DCP setback taxonomy (Bug 2). Behaviour-preserving extraction of the setback-row -> DCPControl mapping into a pure helper, plus a 12-test guard locking the typed-control contract (semantic_type wins over the 'prescribed'/'site_derived' kind) so setbacks keep feeding the footprint calc.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls (the table the engine reads via fetch_dcp_setbacks) is already fully typed: front_setback 97 rows/29 LGAs, side_setback 94/28, rear_setback 77/28, zero 'prescribed'. The only 'prescribed' control_type in the DB is 7 rows in dcp_general_requirements (not setbacks).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Plan assumed setbacks were stored untyped as control_type='prescribed' and needed a pipeline change. DB reality-check disproved this; the only real residual was the untested consumption seam.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new behaviour. The inline mapping at _fetch_constraint_data_from_db was extracted verbatim into _dcp_controls_from_setback_rows() and is now unit-tested in isolation; the DB-coupled caller is unchanged.

functions.name: _dcp_controls_from_setback_rows
functions.input: list of fetch_dcp_setbacks row dicts (setbacks + sd_setbacks) and an optional clause_ref fallback
functions.output: one typed DCPControl per row; control_type from semantic_type, then control_type, then type
functions.if_none: empty input returns []; a row missing semantic_type falls back to control_type (typed in the live DB) then ''

values: N/A - no regulatory values hardcoded; reads extracted DCP values from the row dicts, coercing free-text requirements to a number or keeping them as the condition (never forced into the float field)
queries: N/A - the extracted helper is pure (no DB); the unchanged caller runs the same fetch_dcp_setbacks query as before

break_it.scenario: A setback arrives untyped (only the 'prescribed' kind, no semantic_type)
break_it.what_happens: control_type becomes 'prescribed' and would NOT match a front/rear/side lookup -> silently dropped from the footprint calc (the Bug 2 failure mode)
break_it.how: test_prescribed_only_row_does_not_feed_setbacks asserts the lookup returns None for all three slots — the canary fails loudly if extraction regresses to untyped

break_it.scenario: semantic_type present but control_type carries the 'prescribed' kind
break_it.what_happens: Naive use of control_type would mis-type the setback as 'prescribed'
break_it.how: semantic_type is preferred in the fallback chain; test_semantic_type_beats_prescribed_kind asserts control_type == 'front_setback' and routes into the front slot

break_it.scenario: requirement is free text (no numeric value_min)
break_it.what_happens: Forcing text into the float value_min field would raise or store garbage
break_it.how: _parse_numeric returns None for non-numeric text; test_requirement_freetext_kept_as_condition_not_value asserts value_min is None and the text is preserved as condition

post_merge.manual_verify: None required — pure-logic change, 95/95 constraint tests pass. Optional follow-up (separate thread): confirm whether ca_confidence still caps at medium now that setbacks are typed; if so the cause is unrelated to taxonomy.
